synopsis: Sensors publications provide evidence and methods for lidar simulation: a 2022 stationary dataset spans six months of rain, snow, fog and sunlight for stochastic modeling, calibration and validation, while 2025 mining work combines real and simulated dusty environments in a public database [f4736, f4737, f3953]. A 2022 off-road lidar de-dusting filter reported F1 = 97.55%, but the skeptic’s review qualifies this as performance on its own collected dataset [f7830, f10563]. On-road evidence shows vibration-related lidar position and intensity drift, and strong target-dependent weather effects: aluminium and steel targets were not observed at 20–30 m in specified rain and fog conditions, whereas retroreflective targets retained at least 74% of their clear-weather point count [f4707, f6382, f6383]. The corpus also cites an on-road rain-and-fog simulation model and a credibility-level process, while noting that a 2023 study described earlier degradation demonstrations as simulation-based or limited to sites such as climate chambers [f6381, f8949, f10567]. Beyond lidar modeling, Sensors reports include a 17-participant work-zone VR study with mean wearable-warning responses of approximately 337 ms for vibration, 443 ms for visual cues and 597 ms for audio, plus 2026 examples involving mine non-line-of-sight perception and a vineyard-rover training environment [f3323, f3324, f4121, f4143].

relations.note: Same F1 result; skeptic’s review specifies percent and evaluation on the filter’s own dataset.
